utterances.text: Why was it that the Croatian side opposed your arrival in Dubrovnik on a federal forces ship? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's clear, they definitely opposed that we come in to the Old Town on a federal ship. They even warned us that there might be trouble if we did come in on a federal ship. I think they wanted to make certain that this trip started in Croatian territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please correct me if I'm wrong, but you even viewed the Croatian position on that as a threat at the time?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The result of that particular threat was the fact that you travelled to Dubrovnik -- that your travel to Dubrovnik was organised by the general staff and the Croatian military?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had to give some guarantees -- had to give security guarantees for the travel, which took place through waters very, very close to the Croatian coast. We also had to take a land transport down to Rijeka to do this, so they needed guarantees for that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At the general staff of the Croatian army, you were also told that they would notify officers in Dubrovnik of your arrival, and then those officers would in some way be put in charge of you. What did that mean? What sort of escort did those officers provide?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact there was -- we did not have an escort from the Croatian military. The Krila Dubrovnika, which was the boat we took down, there was no Croatian military on that boat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What exactly were you told? Who was the commander of the Croatian forces in Dubrovnik? Was there something you were told at the general staff?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of General Marinovic came up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What specifically were you told about that?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was the -- he was commanding the Croatian forces in the territory of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ask any questions, general questions - I don't mean detailed questions - about the exact number and deployment of those forces? Did you perhaps express your concern back in Zagreb about the way that General Marinovic's forces were positioned?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall asking any questions about the Croatian forces in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps warn the Croatian side at the Zagreb meeting that it was not allowed to misuse a World Cultural Heritage Site?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm trying to refresh my memory about this. I don't have a -- any memories about this specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Since you can't remember, in view of your role, would it not have been natural for you to draw their attention to the fact that they were to fully and strictly comply with the provisions of the relevant convention?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We explained the mission to them. We explained the -- there -- it was a question of the World Heritage Site, which was Dubrovnik. There was also the question of The Hague Convention. I don't remember -- obviously in The Hague Convention of 1954, if you misuse a cultural site, then there are great risks. I don't recall talking about this particular aspect of The Hague Convention with the Croatian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Once you set out and were on your way, did you realise immediately what the problem could be, what sort of a problem you might be facing once you arrived? On the one hand there is an attack against a protected heritage site, and on the other hand you have someone using this world heritage site to fire back. Did you perhaps think about it in these terms?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just to put it this way, is that I really understood where I was going and what kinds of risks existed when I sat down and watched some of the most recent media reports on -- that had been taped and were shown to us by ECMM. And it was clearly a dangerous place and there could be a lot of shooting. And we saw some things on those reports which -- we saw boats which were supposed to be federal boats. We saw fires burning boats and things like that. I can answer you best by saying we knew it was going to be a dangerous place. All the details of who were shooting at what was not something I was aware of in the detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's how it seems, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I must ask you to return on Monday, Dr. Kaiser. Thank you. We will adjourn for the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: at 1.46 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of February, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.
